submission.natural_language_explanation: L5/H5 copies one token: its near-one-hot attention lands on a single token (the current open-class word, else the nearest content word, else the sequence's first token) and its write is that token's layer-5 value vector, so strength is how far that value sits from the head's mean write. It is therefore active (1.5-4.5) wherever it can latch onto an open-class word - any ordinary sentence, clause or code line in any language, with prose active on about a fifth of tokens and in ~86% of 32-token windows - and inactive (0.3-1.0) where only function words, punctuation or the sequence-initial sink token are reachable: one-word utterances, digit or number-word lists, punctuation or symbol runs, single repeated common words, and lowercase-initial two-to-three-word fragments; capitalised sentence-initial fragments ('The big dog') and repetitions of a rare abstract noun ('discoveries') do cross.

rival_explanations: A lexical token-identity head: it fires on a fixed family of abstract plural nouns (studies, findings, results, observations, recordings) in any context, including bare repetitions, and not on concrete nouns, verbs or code identifiers.

A syntactic subject tracker: it fires at the head noun of a clause subject and the auxiliary or verb that follows it, like a subject-verb-agreement head, and not at objects, adjectives or function words.

A broad any-word reader: it fires on essentially every token that is not a determiner or punctuation, including repeated function words, verbs of any kind and code identifiers, and is silent only on pure symbol or digit strings.
